reason: Both meet all hard requirements (correct headings, snapshot-first gate, no restart/failover before snapshot, explicit abort/rollback), but Response A includes a critical safeguard for the specific scenario described: if disk is projected to hit 100% before the snapshot itself completes, it directs responders to throttle write traffic at the application layer rather than touching the database, buying time without risking data loss. Response B lacks this pre-snapshot safety valve, only introducing write throttling after the snapshot gate has already passed, leaving a gap for the exact near-full, rapidly-degrading scenario in the prompt.
